title: PowerPoint on the web: reference a Teams meeting or chat when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: Hold: the cost rating describes indirect costs only despite the documented Copilot add-on licensing route. The feature description, roadmap details, licence-assignment controls and Teams sensitivity-label limitation are supported.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; rationales
claims.claim: Users can mention a Teams meeting or chat in a prompt and Copilot generates a deck based on that content.
claims.quote: Users can enter a prompt that mentions the relevant Teams meeting or chat, and Copilot will generate a deck based on that content.

claims.claim: Teams discussion content can become presentation content without manual retyping.
claims.quote: This makes it easier to turn Teams conversations, meeting outcomes, and chat discussions into presentation-ready content without manually summarizing or transferring notes.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot surfaces only organisational data the individual user can at least view, using existing Teams and file access boundaries.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot only surfaces organizational data to which individual users have at least view permissions.

claims.claim: Copilot honours user usage rights on data encrypted with Microsoft Purview Information Protection through sensitivity labels or restricted permissions.
claims.quote: When you have data that's encrypted by Microsoft Purview Information Protection, Microsoft Copilot honors the usage rights granted to the user. This encryption can be applied by sensitivity labels or by restricted permissions in apps in Microsoft 365 by using Information Rights Management (IRM).

claims.claim: Copilot does not currently recognize sensitivity labels protecting Teams meetings and chat.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels that protect Teams meetings and chat aren't currently recognized by Copilot and agents.

claims.claim: Returned meeting or channel chat data does not display the associated sensitivity label.
claims.quote: data returned from a meeting chat or channel chat won't display an associated sensitivity label

claims.claim: Those Teams sensitivity labels cannot prevent copying returned chat data to a destination item.
claims.quote: copying chat data can't be prevented for a destination item

claims.claim: The Teams meeting or chat sensitivity label cannot be inherited by the destination.
claims.quote: the sensitivity label can't be inherited

claims.claim: The limitation does not apply to sensitivity-labelled meeting invites, responses and calendar events.
claims.quote: This limitation doesn't apply to meeting invites, responses, and calendar events that are protected by sensitivity labels.

claims.claim: The release notes describe presentation creation after a user enters the referencing prompt and presses Enter.
claims.quote: Enter a prompt that references the Teams meeting or chat you want to use in your presentation. ... Press Enter. Copilot will create a presentation using the referenced Teams content.

claims.claim: No new identity or permission model is described for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot Teams meeting chat presentation autonomous actions identity permissions. Opened release-notes feature entry and microsoft-365-copilot-privacy; entry describes a user prompt, privacy states current-user access boundaries, not a new identity.

claims.claim: The documentation read does not describe this referencing feature taking actions outside the presentation.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot Teams meeting chat presentation autonomous actions identity permissions. Opened release-notes feature entry, microsoft-365-copilot-privacy and configure-copilot-admin-center; no outside-presentation action documented for this feature.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published how this feature matches a referenced meeting or chat to the prompt.
claims.quote: Searched: "PowerPoint" "meeting" "matched" "Copilot"; PowerPoint Agent Mode reference Teams meeting chat admin disable setting licensing transcript matching prompt. Opened release-notes entry; it says to reference the meeting or chat, without describing matching.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions

claims.claim: No separate meter or feature charge is published in the licensing page or this release-notes entry.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint reference Teams meeting chat presentation Agent Mode license Copilot Chat meter charge. Opened microsoft-365-copilot-licensing and release-notes entry; read pay-as-you-go-meters search excerpt. None names a separate meter or charge for this feature.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Assigning licences in the Microsoft 365 admin center requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: User licence assignment is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: go to the Users > Active users page. ... Select the row of the user ... In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. ... Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a product licence using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. ... Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: The row is a general user-level licence-assignment control, not a feature-specific referencing switch.
claims.quote: When you use the Active users page to assign or unassign licenses, you assign or unassign users licenses to products.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The default state is user-opt-in: users choose to use the capability by referencing a meeting or chat in a prompt.
claims.quote: Users can enter a prompt that mentions the relevant Teams meeting or chat, and Copilot will generate a deck based on that content.
